title: Starlake Dynamics - PLG onramp & hosting-fit discussion
summary: Intro discovery focused on self-serve quickstart, free credits, and deciding between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a prototype. Discussed time-to-first-token, basic security needs (SSO, SOC2), and cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed to run a short pilot using hosted credits and share security pack + billing details.
topics: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
security checklist: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
latency vs cost, batching and token pricing
next steps: credentials, pilot criteria, benchmark plan
transcript:
[00:00:00] Elliot Shaw: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Elliot, AE at Redwood. Priya from our SE team is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Maya Chen: Good, thanks. We're excited, short on time but wanted to focus on quickstart and whether we can go hosted to get to first token fast.
[00:00:20] Priya Nair: Great. We'll run through the self-serve flow, free credits, and then dig into hosting choices. Quick note up front: the credits typically cover N calls depending on model and tokens, we'll give you a rough estimate.
[00:00:35] Omar Ruiz: Awesome. Our main problem is we need sub-200ms text generation for a demo but don't want to blow budget. Also we're evaluating private for PII concerns.
[00:00:48] Lena Park: And from infra side I'd like to know what's required for VPC vs Dedicated — e.g., can we move from hosted to dedicated without code changes?
[00:00:58] Elliot Shaw: Short answer: yes, same API surface. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. Migration path is intentionally smooth.
[00:01:06] Priya Nair: We'll show the SDK snippet in a sec. For latency, hosted can be fast — depends on model and region — but Dedicated gives more predictable p99s. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance and data residency.
[00:01:25] Maya Chen: What's the typical time-to-first-token if we sign up and use free credits?
[00:01:31] Priya Nair: From sign-up to first request: often under an hour for a basic quickstart app. With our quickstart templates you can hit a sample call in ~10-20 minutes if you have a dev laptop. For more integrated flows (SSO, VPC), expect days to a couple weeks depending on approvals.
[00:01:50] Omar Ruiz: Are there sandbox API keys or are they real paid tokens?
[00:01:54] Elliot Shaw: They're credit-backed billing keys tied to your account. They won't charge you until credits are used up and you add billing. Credits expire after 90 days by default, we can adjust on a case-by-case.
[00:02:08] Priya Nair: (mumbles) Also note rate limits apply on free tiers but we can increase for pilot.
[00:02:15] Maya Chen: Good. Security: we need SOC2 in vendor pack, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration for keys — anything else?
[00:02:23] Priya Nair: That's the usual list. We also have audit logs, RBAC, and optional HSM/KMS integration for Private deployments. For Hosted customers we offer customer managed keys via KMS in dedicated/private options; hosted has server-side encryption and enterprise KMS add-ons.
[00:02:41] Lena Park: Can you share the SOC2 evidence and the network diagram?
[00:02:45] Elliot Shaw: Absolutely — we'll send the security pack after the call. It's in our docs and we can set an NDA if needed.
[00:02:52] Omar Ruiz: On models — we're going to evaluate a 7B open model and a smaller 3B for latency; do you host any quantized variants?
[00:02:59] Priya Nair: We onboard model variants and have quantized variants available; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per workload. For the 3B you should see much lower token cost and latency.
[00:03:10] Maya Chen: Do you provide performance benchmarks or sample tokens-per-second numbers?
[00:03:14] Priya Nair: We publish model profiles and per-region latency stats, and we can run a short benchmark on your prompt set as part of the pilot. That will give you exact p50/p95/p99.
[00:03:24] Lena Park: If we go hosted for the pilot and later need private for production, what's the migration plan and downtime?
[00:03:30] Elliot Shaw: Migration is configuration-driven; you can re-route traffic to Dedicated or Private with minimal code changes. Rolling deploys and canary policies reduce risk; there's no forced downtime but you'll want to plan cutover windows for KV cache warmups.
[00:03:46] Omar Ruiz: Cache warmups — is KV cache preserved across deployments?
[00:03:49] Priya Nair: Not automatically across different infra types. Within the same deployment cluster we preserve caches but moving from hosted to a new Dedicated cluster will need some warmup strategy — we can pre-populate with prefixes during the pilot.
[00:03:59] Maya Chen: Pricing: how do we estimate token spend for a prototype?
[00:04:03] Elliot Shaw: We can model it — give us your expected QPS and average token length and we can produce cost per 10k calls. Also Redwood Optimize suggests batching to reduce per-token compute.
[00:04:15] Priya Nair: For demo-level usage, most teams keep costs low by selecting smaller models and batching; the quickstart credit is usually enough to validate feature parity.
[00:04:26] Lena Park: Are there limits in the quickstart that would block real API usage? e.g., limited endpoints or no streaming?
[00:04:32] Priya Nair: Quickstart supports streaming, function-calls, embeddings — pretty much the full API. Some enterprise-only ops (long-term retention beyond default, certain compliance add-ons) require an enterprise plan.
[00:04:45] Omar Ruiz: One thing — we've had hallucination concerns, do you support reranking or safety hooks?
[00:04:50] Priya Nair: Yes, you can run reranking pipelines and Redwood supports filter hooks and evals to catch regressions. We also integrate with your monitoring to alert on quality regressions.
[00:05:02] Maya Chen: OK sounds good. Can we talk about timeline? We want a demo-ready prototype in four weeks; is that realistic?
[00:05:08] Elliot Shaw: Four weeks is doable. Typical plan: week 0-1 sign up and quickstart using credits, week 2 run benchmark and iterate on prompts/models, week 3 integrate SSO and observability, week 4 demo and evaluate Dedicated/private needs.
[00:05:21] Lena Park: Who needs to be involved from Redwood to move quickly?
[00:05:25] Elliot Shaw: AE + SE pair (that's us) plus solutions engineering for a pilot benchmark if you want custom infra. We'll also pull security if you request SOC2 artifacts.
[00:05:35] Omar Ruiz: For the quickstart, do you have SDK samples in Python and JS?
[00:05:38] Priya Nair: Yes, we have both and several templated examples for chat, QA, and embeddings. We'll link the repo.
[00:05:44] Maya Chen: Are we allowed to spin up multiple projects under one org for environment separation?
[00:05:49] Elliot Shaw: Yep, multi-project and team RBAC is supported.
[00:05:52] Priya Nair: Quick note: if you expect spikes in demo environment, we can set burst capacity and we can increase rate limits for pilot windows.
[00:06:00] Maya Chen: How long do credits last? You said 90 days — can you extend if we have a delayed launch?
[00:06:06] Elliot Shaw: We can make exceptions; we'll check with growth ops.
[00:06:09] Lena Park: For security review, can we run a quick checklist now?
[00:06:13] Maya Chen: (overlapping) We need SSO, audit logs, data deletion policy, data residency.
[00:06:18] Priya Nair: We track audit logs, support SAML and SCIM provisioning, we have a documented data deletion process and retention TTLs. For residency we offer Private deployments or region selection for Hosted.
[00:06:30] Omar Ruiz: Also curious about model versioning — we want ability to pin to a known-good model.
[00:06:35] Priya Nair: You can pin model versions and set rollout policies; you can also do A/B traffic splits and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant.
[00:06:43] Maya Chen: Great. Can Redwood run a mini-benchmark with our prompts?
[00:06:47] Elliot Shaw: Yes — if you share a small prompt set (50-100 prompts) we can run it against two model variants and return latency and token-cost numbers within 3 business days.
[00:06:58] Omar Ruiz: Perfect. About SDKs: do you provide auto-reconnect and streaming reassembly? We need robust streaming for demo.
[00:07:04] Priya Nair: Our SDK handles streaming and has utilities to reassemble chunks; the REST interface supports chunked responses too.
[00:07:11] Lena Park: For the pilot, we want to test 100 RPS for short bursts — will hosted credits let us do that?
[00:07:18] Elliot Shaw: For short bursts yes, we can enable higher burst limits for the pilot. Sustained high RPS is where Dedicated helps.
[00:07:25] Maya Chen: Any hidden costs or data transfer fees?
[00:07:28] Elliot Shaw: No hidden token surcharges; standard compute + per-token pricing. If you use Private with cross-region networking there may be network egress charges from your cloud provider.
[00:07:38] Omar Ruiz: Competitors question: we've been looking at OpenAI and Anthropic — how are you different on dev experience and cost?
[00:07:44] Elliot Shaw: We focus on predictable inference economics and cross-environment parity — same API for hosted/dedicated/private — and we include tooling for rollouts, caching and quantization recommendations to lower unit cost.
[00:07:57] Maya Chen: Ok, logistics: can you send a one-pager pilot plan and the security pack?
[00:08:02] Elliot Shaw: Yes. We'll send both and a quickstart link.
[00:08:05] Priya Nair: I'll also include the SDK samples and an example benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:08:10] (meeting continues with back-and-forth; some side chatter and clarifying prompts)
[00:30:12] Maya Chen: Sorry jumped ahead — a couple specific items: is there a free tier rate-limited to 20rpm? We've seen that elsewhere.
[00:30:19] Elliot Shaw: Our free credit API keys do have rate-limits but not a fixed 20rpm; it's a soft limit that scales. For the pilot we'll open a higher window.
[00:37:40] Omar Ruiz: Minor typo in the doc — you said 10k calls for X credits? Might be 1k.
[00:37:44] Priya Nair: Thanks, we'll double-check the cost estimate in the follow-up email.
[00:43:55] Lena Park: Last question — do you support bringing our own models to Dedicated?
[00:43:59] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated and Private can host customer models, subject to onboarding and compatibility checks. We'll need your model artifact and some metadata.
[00:44:08] Elliot Shaw: Wrap up: we'll share security pack, pilot one-pager, link to quickstart, and set up the benchmark run once we have your prompt set.
[00:44:18] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone.
[00:44:21] Elliot Shaw: Thanks, we'll follow up with the materials and a proposed timeline.
